info: This is the master music_rules file
help: RCM Levels 5-7 music theory rhythm rules.

dedfinitions.name: simple time
dedfinitions.definition: The top number is the number of beats in each measure. The bottom is the value of the note that receives one beat

dedfinitions.name: compound time
dedfinitions.definition: The top number is the number of pulses in each measure. The bottom is the value of the note that receives one pulse
dedfinitions.details: The pulses are grouped in threes. Each group of 3 pulses is felt as one beat

dedfinitions.name: compound duple meter
dedfinitions.details: 6/4: dotted half beat, quarter note pulse; 6/8: dotted quarter beat, 8th note pulse, 6/16: dotted 8th beat, 16th note pulse

dedfinitions.name: compound triple meter
dedfinitions.details: 9/4: dotted half beat, quarter note pulse

dedfinitions.name: compound quadruple meter
dedfinitions.details: 12/4: dotted half beat, quarter note pulse

rule_list.rule: A whole rest is used for a full measure of silence in both simple and compound time
A breve rest is sometimes used for a full measure of silence in 4/2, 9/4, and 12/4
In compound time, dotted rests are used to show a full beat
rule_list.details: the rest value is twice the pulse value
rule_list.examples: 6/4 - dotted half, 6/8 - dotted quarter, 6/16 - dotted eighth

rule_list.rule: A strong beat can be combined with weaker beats that follow
rule_list.examples: 9/8 (S-w-w): dotted half rest (S-w), dotted quarter note

rule_list.rule: A weak beat cannot be combined with a weak beat that follows
A weak beat cannot be combined with a medium beat that follows
In duple and quadruple meters, you must combine two rests into one when both rests are in the first half or second half of the measure
rule_list.details: applies to 2/4, 4/2 (whole rest), 4/4 (half rest), 12/4 (dotted whole rest), 12/8, 12/16

rule_list.rule: In triple meter rests on beats 1 and 2 can either be shown separately or combined
rule_list.details: Beats 2 and 3 are both weak, and so rests on beats 2 and 3 cannot be combined

rules.name: adding rests to measures in compound time

rule_list.rule: In compound time dotted rests are used to show a full beat
Each pulse must be completed before continuing to fill in any additional pulses with silence
Treat the 3 pulses of each beat as you would treat a measure in simple triple time
A weak pulse cannot be combined with another weak pulse
A weak pulse cannot be combined with a strong or medium pulse that follows
The 1st two pulses of each beat may be combined as one rest, but the second and 3rd may not
Build a series of half steps using accidentals to raise notes when ascending and to lower them when descending
Use a bar line after the upper tonic to cancel all previously used accidentals
Don't use more than 2 note with the same letter name consecutively within the ascending or descending segment
Don't change the starting note enharmonically
Generally a whole-tone scale is notated using either sharps or flats but not a mixure of both
Build a series of whole steps using accidentals as required
Don't change the starting note enharmonically
The octatonic scale consists of 8 different pitches that alternate half steps and whole steps
rule_list.details: There are 3 possible forms or transpositions. Pattern is H-W-H-W-H-W-H-W or W-H-W-H-W-H-W-H

rule_list.rule: One of the half steps will be written as a chromatic half step
Don't change the starting note enharmonically
Write a major scale, omiting 4 (subdominant) and 7 (leading tone)
Resulting pattern is maj 2, maj 2, min 3, maj 2, min 3
Write a major scale, omiting 2 (supertonic) and 6 (submediant)
Resulting pattern is min 3, maj 2, maj 2, min 3, maj 2
Write a minor pentatonic scale, adding either a #4 or b5
Resulting pattern is min 3, maj 2, min 2, min 2, min 3, maj 2

procedures.name: adding rests to measures in compound time

steps.1: Draw a diagram (below the staff) showing the main beats and pulses

steps.2: Mark the strong and weak beats

steps.5: Fill in any missing beats using dotted rests
